meta.title: Why Dozify — What It Does and What It Refuses To
meta.description: Built for people already prescribed a GLP-1. It records what you and your doctor decide; it does not suggest doses or interpret results.

strings: Five things this app is built around. Each one is a claim you can check against how it behaves.
Your records stay on your phone

Doses, weights, side effects and photos are stored in a database on your device. Usage analytics never carries a medication name or a symptom, and progress photos are never uploaded anywhere. The one photo that does leave the phone is a meal photo you choose to analyse with AI calories: it goes, after you agree, through our server to Google Gemini for the estimate and is not stored by the app. The privacy policy lists exactly what leaves the device and why.

The home screen is built from the things you said you care about: cards can be reordered, hidden, or brought back whenever you like. An app that shows everyone everything is an app nobody reads. If food matters to you, the AI meal card turns a photo into an editable calorie and protein draft; if you take a tablet, the pill tracker follows a daily rhythm.

Every article in the education section names where it came from (MedlinePlus (NIH), FDA, NIDDK, TİTCK) and links straight to it. Dozify is a tracking tool: it does not recommend doses and does not interpret results.
Suggestions arrive as mail read by the person who writes the app, from Settings → Suggest a feature or at support@dozify.app. There is no ticket queue in between.
Fixes and additions ship as they are ready, and each release says what changed. Most of what has been added since launch started as a message from someone using the app.
